Official bare-earth DTM covering about 99% of England at 1m, EPSG:27700 and published ±0.15m RMSE.
Metadata does not prove current WCS bytes, row-specific lineage or confidence.
EA publishes the persistent DTM1m WCS 2.0.1 endpoint and describes WCS as raw-pixel access.
The support runtime observed application/xml but could not retrieve raw XML bytes because container DNS failed and the web reader rejects XML.
Official 2m bare-earth product provides a resolution-sensitivity comparator.
It cannot replace the pinned 1m metric.
Official 10m DTM is resampled from the 2m composite and supplies coarse context.
It is unsuitable for parcel-scale sub-metre measurement.
Official DSM includes buildings, vegetation and other surface objects.
DSM is a negative control and must not be promoted as bare-earth terrain.
EA exposes survey downloads and temporal survey context for LiDAR coverage.
Survey availability does not prove which survey contributed to a current composite pixel without a row-bound lineage receipt.
Open indicative freehold polygons are split by local authority and use unique Land Registry-INSPIRE IDs.
Polygons are not legal title plans and can be duplicated across authority boundaries.
Current files were published 5 July 2026; Enfield, Havering and Lambeth are listed and replacement occurs on the first Sunday monthly.
Search-index evidence confirms catalogue presence but not exact package bytes or hashes.
HMLR states polygons are captured against British National Grid and reprojection may shift features by up to 15m.
The matcher must require native EPSG:27700 or block transformed exceptions.
The dataset is monthly GML and current files remain available until the next publication.
Lifecycle metadata must be bound to authority filename, download address and content hash.
The official endpoint returns available OpenData products as application/json and supports expanded details.
Documentation does not prove a current response body or product hash.
A product identifier can be resolved to a specific current product record.
The current resolver does not require a separate product-details receipt.
Downloads can be filtered by filename, format, subformat and National Grid area; redirect occurs for exactly one match.
Selected record, final HTTPS host and archive bytes must all be verified.
OS documents comparing product versions and retrieving product-specific download lists.
Example automation does not replace fail-closed provenance, content-type, size and hash controls.
OS Terrain 50 is free OpenData, updated annually in July and supplied as grid and contours.
It is a secondary landscape-scale check rather than a parcel metric.
Grid data uses regular 50m posts and 10km-by-10km tiles identified by the south-west National Grid reference.
Tile identity must be verified against raster bounds and headers.
Technical specification defines the product supply formats and processing contract.
Specification text alone does not establish archive integrity.
Each tile has 200 rows, 200 columns and 50m cells; values are pixel-centre heights to 0.1m and companion files are defined.
Crosschecker must enforce header, schema, companion and tile-bound contracts.
Per-tile metadata identifies the product, tile, EPSG:27700, EPSG:5701 and flying-date range.
Metadata must be paired and hashed with the exact raster and projection files.
National tiled supply has 2,858 10km tiles in 55 folders and is fully resupplied annually in July.
Multiple editions of one tile must not be concatenated.
Terrain grid heights are pixel-centre values and adjacent tile edges are not duplicated.
This does not permit duplicate archive members or duplicate editions.
Terrain 50 is interpolated and generalised from a bare-earth TIN; most heights use Newlyn Datum.
Observed datum metadata and secondary-source role remain mandatory.
WCS separates GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage and GetCoverage and binds coverage domain and range structures.
Client must validate service/version, selected coverage, domain, axes and range rather than trust request parameters.
The extension permits explicit client control of interpolation.
